title: Karaage Crispy Japanese Fried Chicken

seo.title: Karaage Recipe: Crispy Japanese Fried Chicken
seo.metaDescription: Master the art of crispy Karaage! This authentic Japanese fried chicken recipe guarantees tender, juicy bites with an irresistible crunch. Perfect for home cooks!
seo.h1: Karaage: The Ultimate Crispy Japanese Fried Chicken Recipe
seo.imageAlt: Plate of golden crispy Karaage Japanese fried chicken with lemon and a side of dipping sauce.
seo.imageCaption: Dive into the deliciousness of homemade Karaage! Perfectly crispy and incredibly flavorful Japanese fried chicken.

description: Karaage is a beloved Japanese fried chicken, known for its incredible crispiness and juicy, flavorful meat. Marinated in a savory blend of soy sauce, ginger, and garlic, each bite offers a delightful crunch followed by tender chicken. This recipe will guide you to achieve perfectly golden-brown Karaage, a true taste of Japan.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces, roughly 1.5 inches. Pat them dry thoroughly with paper towels to ensure a crispy coating. Place the chicken in a medium bowl.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a separate small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, sake, mirin, grated ginger, grated garlic, and sesame oil to create the marinade. Pour this mixture over the chicken pieces, ensuring all pieces are well coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for deeper flavor.

instructions.title: Coat the Chicken
instructions.text: After marinating, add the beaten egg to the chicken and mix well until each piece is coated. In a shallow dish, spread out the potato starch. Take each chicken piece and dredge it thoroughly in the potato starch, pressing gently to ensure a thick, even coating. Shake off any excess starch.

instructions.title: First Fry
instructions.text: Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 340F (170C). Carefully add the chicken pieces in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot. Fry for about 2-3 minutes until the chicken is lightly golden and cooked through. Remove the chicken with a slotted spoon and place it on a wire rack set over a baking sheet to drain. Repeat with remaining batches.

instructions.title: Rest the Chicken
instructions.text: Allow all the first-fried chicken pieces to rest on the wire rack for at least 5-10 minutes. This resting period allows the internal temperature to equalize and prepares the chicken for the second fry, which will achieve ultimate crispiness.

instructions.title: Second Fry for Crispy Finish
instructions.text: Increase the oil temperature to 375F (190C). Return the rested chicken pieces to the hot oil in batches, frying for another 1-2 minutes until they are deep golden brown and exceptionally crispy. Remove from oil and place back on the wire rack to drain any excess oil.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Serve the crispy Karaage hot, garnished with fresh lemon wedges. The lemon juice adds a refreshing zest that perfectly complements the rich flavors of the fried chicken. Enjoy as a main dish, appetizer, or bento box component.

tips: For the crispiest Karaage, always double-fry. The first fry cooks the chicken, and the second, at a higher temperature, creates the signature crunchy exterior.
Using potato starch (katakuriko) is key for authentic Karaage crispiness. It creates a lighter, airier crust compared to flour or cornstarch.
Serve Karaage immediately after the second fry for optimal crispiness. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice brightens the flavor beautifully.
